beats.t: This village is in the middle of a desert, and it hasn't rained here in months.
But the people here have fresh, cold water every single day. Without a single pump.
The secret starts way over there, at the foot of those mountains.
First, they dig a deep well, until they hit groundwater. This is called the mother well.
Then, starting from the village, they dig a tunnel all the way toward it.
Digging a tunnel that long is a nightmare. So every few dozen meters, they dig a vertical shaft.
The shafts bring in fresh air, let the diggers haul out the dirt, and keep the tunnel on track.
Now here's the clever part. The tunnel slopes down very gently, just enough for water to flow by gravity.
Too steep, and the rushing water would tear the tunnel apart. Too flat, and the water would just sit there.
Once the tunnel reaches the mother well, the water starts to flow.
It travels deep underground, where the desert sun can't evaporate it.
And it comes out right in the middle of the village, cold and clean.
From there, it fills the pools, waters the fields, and turns the whole village green.
This is called a qanat. People in ancient Persia were building them thousands of years ago.
Some are still running today. The Persian qanat is even a UNESCO World Heritage site.
All of that, from a few holes in the ground and the perfect slope.
